summary: Jordan issues most nationalities a single-entry visa on arrival for JOD 40 allowing a 30-day stay, and waives that fee entirely for travelers who buy the Jordan Pass (which bundles Petra and 40+ sites) and stay at least two nights (3 days), according to the official Jordan Pass site — while about 50 nationalities, most of them African and Asian, need prior approval from the Ministry of Interior or an embassy visa.

conditionalWaivers.text: Ordinary-passport holders who live in a GCC country — or in the US, Canada, Australia, Japan, South Korea, the EU, the Nordic countries or the UK — can get a visa on arrival without the Ministry of Interior's prior approval, provided their residence permit is valid for at least 6 more months; arrivals by air must also hold a return ticket. The same applies to holders of a Schengen or US visa valid for at least 6 months. Nationals of Nigeria, Iran and Bangladesh, and holders of travel documents, still need prior approval.

source.name: Jordan Ministry of Interior — FAQ (entry of residents of foreign countries; nationalities needing prior approval)

fee.notes: The Ministry of Tourism's Jordan Pass site says the fee is waived if you buy the pass before arrival and stay at least two nights (3 days); the UK Foreign Office gives the minimum as 3 nights. The same site says the fee is also waived for travelers who enter at the Wadi Araba border, stay at least 2 nights and leave by the same border, and lists South Africa, Malaysia, Hong Kong, Japan and Vatican City as nationalities exempt from the fee.

Canada's travel advice says penalties for illegal drugs are severe: even small amounts are a criminal offence, and you could be held for up to 2 weeks without charge.

payments.text: The UK Foreign Office says most places accept card payments but cash machines are widely available only in Amman and other major towns. Canada's travel advice says larger stores and restaurants in Amman and tourist areas accept credit cards, ATMs are limited outside the larger cities and Queen Alia airport, and only US dollars and euros are easily converted into dinars.

safety.text: The FCDO reports Iranian strikes in Jordan since 8 July 2026, with renewed attacks and interceptions in and around Aqaba in early September, and warns of short-notice airspace closures. It advises against all travel within 3 km of the Syrian border. It advises staying away from military sites and strategic infrastructure, and following local instructions to shelter.

bestTimeToVisit.text: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Jordan. Canada's travel advice says the rainy season usually runs from November to March, with a risk of flash floods in wadis and on roads, and that snowfall is infrequent but can close roads.

idp.text: Jordan is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

tips.text: The Ministry of Tourism's Jordan Pass site sells three passes, from 70 to 80 JD, with one to three days at Petra and free entry to over 40 attractions; the tourist visa fee is waived if you buy the pass before arrival and stay at least two nights (3 days). The UK Foreign Office gives the minimum as 3 nights and advises buying the pass only from the official website.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Jordan?
faq.answer: Yes, but it is issued on arrival: a single-entry visa costs JOD 40 and is valid for one month. The UK Foreign Office says a visit visa can be extended online for up to 6 months. The Ministry of Tourism's Jordan Pass site says the visa fee is waived if you buy the pass before arrival and stay at least two nights (3 days).

faq.question: Is the Jordan Pass worth it?
faq.answer: The Ministry of Tourism's Jordan Pass site sells three passes — 70 JD (one day at Petra), 75 JD (two consecutive days) and 80 JD (three consecutive days) — each with free entry to over 40 attractions, and the tourist visa fee is waived if you buy it before arrival and stay at least two nights (3 days).

faq.question: How do I pay for the Jordan visa on arrival?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states how the visa-on-arrival fee is paid. The Ministry of Tourism's Jordan Pass site says pass holders present the pass at the airport visa office to have the fee waived, and should show it printed out because the QR code may not scan from a phone.

faq.question: Can I stay in Jordan longer than 30 days?
faq.answer: Yes. The Jordan Tourism Board says the visa can be extended at any police station, and the UK Foreign Office says a visit visa can be extended online for up to 6 months and that you could be fined if you overstay.

faq.question: Can Indian citizens get a visa on arrival in Jordan?
faq.answer: Yes. India is not on the Ministry of Interior's list of restricted nationalities — the ones that need prior approval — and the Jordan Tourism Board says unrestricted nationalities can get a visa at Queen Alia International Airport or any other border crossing except King Hussein Bridge.
